14 Which relationship is used in the derivation of the equation shown?
power = force  velocity
A
displacement = velocity  time
B
force = mass  acceleration
C
momentum = mass  velocity
D
velocity = acceleration  time

hints: Start from the definitions present in the question: power is work divided by time and work is force multiplied by displacement.
Look for a relationship that lets you replace displacement $s$ with something containing velocity $v$ in $P = F s / t$.
Check which option gives $s = v t$ so that time $t$ cancels to leave force multiplied by velocity.
walkthrough: Recall the defining equations: power $P = W / t$ and work done by a constant force $W = F s$, where $s$ is displacement in the direction of the force.
Combine them to get $P = F s / t$.
To obtain velocity $v$ in the final $power = force \times velocity$ form, displacement must be expressed using velocity and time.
Use $displacement = velocity \times time$, or $s = v t$, valid for constant velocity.
Substitute: $P = F (v t) / t = F v$, with time cancelling. This is option A.

A.explanation: Substituting $s = v t$ into $P = F s / t$ cancels $t$ to leave $P = F v$.

B.explanation: Newton's second law $F = m a$ is not needed because the derivation uses work and displacement, not mass.

C.explanation: Momentum $p = m v$ does not appear in the work definition $W = F s$ used to obtain power.

D.explanation: $v = a t$ applies to uniformly accelerated motion but power derivation needs displacement in terms of steady velocity.
